passages.title: Secure heights cannot excuse betrayal of a brother
passages.summary: Obadiah’s vision concerns Edom, the nation descended from Esau. Edom lives high in the rocks and thinks no one can bring it down. God will bring it down. Its allies will deceive it, and its wise men will perish. Edom did violence to its brother Jacob. It stood aside while strangers looted Jerusalem. It gloated, entered the gates, and seized goods. It cut down those who fled, and what it did will be done to it.
passages.uncertainty: Markers locate selected geographic references. The vision does not establish a traveled route.

lds.text: The 2026 lesson applies the final verse to temple service for deceased people. This later Church reading differs from the vision’s judgment over Edom. Why does intercepting people who escape make Edom part of the violence?

contextNote.title: Secure heights cannot excuse betrayal of a brother
contextNote.text: Verses 11–14 follow Edom’s conduct step by step. First it stood aside while Jerusalem was looted. Then it gloated, entered the city, and took plunder. Verse 14 names the last step. Edom waited at the crossroads for those who had escaped. It killed some and handed over the rest. Verse 10 calls the victim “your brother Jacob,” which makes it betrayal.
